title: id(world): many_worlds p99 is blocking fdatasync on Tokio workers, capped at ~1.5k commits/s (not algorithmic)

body:
## What

The F11.8 \`many_worlds\` reference measurement (\`benches/BASELINES.md\`, #557) misses its p99 target: 5,650.8 ms vs 50 ms, with completed throughput 1,523.1/s against 2,000/s scheduled. The cause is **not** an algorithmic O(n) problem in the journal. Each durable commit runs a synchronous \`fdatasync\` on a Tokio worker thread, so concurrent commits are capped at the worker count and the rest queue.

## Evidence

**Per-append path** (no O(journal) work — checked):

- \`src/world/actor.rs:444-469\` — \`WorldActor::persist\` is synchronous and calls \`journal.append\` inline from the actor task.
- \`src/world_store.rs:184-204\` — \`FileJournal::append\`: one \`write_all\`, then \`self.file.sync_data()\` at **:202**. No directory fsync, no re-read, no re-encode of the journal.
- Per input: 1 fsync, 1 write, 3 full JSON encodes (\`actor.rs:482-485\` for replication, \`core.rs:29-31\` / \`:1983-1985\` for admin-history sizing, plus the journal line), and ~4 event clones (\`actor.rs:1370\`, \`core.rs:1964,1968\`).

**Concurrency cap** (\`benches/world_bench.rs:704-708\`): the runtime is \`new_multi_thread().worker_threads(available_parallelism())\` = 16 on the reference laptop. The bench drives 100 active worlds at 20 commits/s = **2,000 fsyncs/s**. Each fsync blocks one worker, so at most 16 are ever in flight.

**Micro-benchmark** (same filesystem, 64-byte appends to 100 files, \`fdatasync\` timed):

| concurrency | fsync/s | p50 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 thread | 168 | 5.5 ms |
| 16 | 1,190–1,456 | — |
| 32 | 2,083 | — |
| 64 | 2,648 | — |

The bench's 1,523 completed/s sits at the 16-way ceiling. Backlog ≈ (2000−1523)/1523 ≈ 3 s, which matches the p99.

**Secondary (smaller, same area):**

- \`src/world/core.rs:503-506\` — open re-serializes every journal entry with \`serde_json::to_vec\` just to charge the memory budget, on the async worker.
- \`src/world_store.rs:416-421\` — \`WorldCore::restore_with_runtime\` runs on the runtime worker in \`open_world\`, while \`FileJournal::open\` is offloaded.
- \`src/world_hub.rs:601-622\` — eviction shuts victims down before the requested world opens (\`:539-541\`), serialising leases behind the victim's in-flight command.

## Proposed fix (ranked)

1. **Take the fsync off the runtime worker.** Give \`FileJournal\` a dedicated writer thread (request channel → write + \`fdatasync\` → reply) so \`WorldJournal::append\` keeps its contract and ordering. Do not use \`block_in_place\`: \`FileJournal\` is also called from \`spawn_blocking\` during open. Estimated 40–50 lines. Expected to lift the cap from ~1.5k to ~2.5k fsyncs/s.
2. **Group commit.** One flusher writes all pending per-world appends and issues one \`syncfs(2)\` per batch. This is the only design that reliably sustains 2,000 durable events/s under 50 ms p99 on this device. Risky (per-world error attribution, compaction ordering, replication snapshots), so it deserves its own design doc per \`pkgs/id/AGENTS.md\`.
3. Move \`restore_with_runtime\` into the existing \`spawn_blocking\` in \`open_world\` and drop the redundant encode/clones listed above.

## Acceptance

- \`cargo bench --bench world_bench\` on the reference machine: \`many_worlds\` p99 < 50 ms, or a recorded result with the target still missed and a reason.
- \`journal_append_fsync\` baseline unchanged (5.18 ms/append) or explained.
- Checkpoint/eviction/reopen assertions in \`many_worlds\` still pass.

Related: #557 (the target this measurement belongs to). Found while profiling for PR #5500 (Bolt, #5489); not addressed there.
